title: Event Monitoring notification channels: email, webhook and Amazon SNS setup and verification

checks.do: Before creating an SNS subscription, whether sns:verify returned 200 with verified true for the topic ARN.
For a 422 from sns:verify, whether the topic exists and its policy lets the Zscaler role call sns:GetTopicAttributes and sns:Publish.
For an email or webhook subscription that never fires, whether the address matches the channel's validation pattern and the webhook is reachable.

channel-operations.statement: The contract has five channel operations: GET /subscriptions/channels, GET on /subscriptions/channels/email, /webhook and /sns, and POST /subscriptions/channels/sns:verify.

expect.operationId: Subscription Resource Verify Sns Topic Access

channel-list.statement: GET /subscriptions/channels lists the channel types supported for the tenant, each with `type`, `description` and `setup_required`; SNS shows `setup_required: true`, meaning more configuration is needed before it can be used.

quotes: Use GET /subscriptions/channels to retrieve the list of all notification channel types supported for your tenant, shown as follows.
"description": "Email notifications",
The sns entry with "setup_required": true indicates that additional configuration is needed before you can use the SNS channel.

evidence.after: Use GET /subscriptions/channels to retrieve the list of all notification channel types supported for your tenant, shown as follows.
quotes: "type": "email",
"setup_required": false,

validation-rules.statement: Email addresses in `email.to`, `cc` and `bcc` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$`, and `webhook_url` must match `^https?://.+$`.

quotes: | Email | email.to/cc/bcc | Must match: ^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$ |
| Webhook | webhook_url | Must match: ^https?://.+$ |

sns-cross-account.statement: Zscaler publishes to the customer's SNS topic from a Zscaler-managed AWS account using an assumed IAM role, and the customer controls who can publish through the topic policy.

quotes: Cross‑account publishing: Zscaler publishes messages to your SNS topic from a Zscaler‑managed AWS account using an assumed Identity and Access Management (IAM) role associated with your AWS account.
Customer‑managed permissions: You control who can publish to your SNS topic via an SNS topic policy

sns-details.statement: GET /subscriptions/channels/sns returns the Zscaler IAM role ARN (`zscaler_role_arn`), the required permissions (`sns:Publish` and `sns:GetTopicAttributes` in the example) and an SNS topic policy template (`sns_topic_policy_template`) to apply to the topic.

quotes: Use GET /subscriptions/channels/sns to retrieve the Zscaler IAM role ARN, the minimum required permissions, and a ready‑to‑use SNS topic policy template that you can apply to your SNS topic.
"zscaler_role_arn": "arn:aws:iam::590183682394:role/CNS-SNS-Publisher",
"required_permissions": [
Use sns_topic_policy_template when configuring your SNS topic policy in the next step.
"sns:Publish",
"sns:GetTopicAttributes"

sns-regions.statement: The SNS channel supports any AWS commercial region where SNS is available.

quotes: Region support: The SNS channel supports any AWS commercial region where SNS is available.

verify-request.statement: POST /subscriptions/channels/sns:verify takes a required `topic_arn` matching `arn:aws:sns:<region>:<12-digit-account>:<topic-name>` (optional .fifo suffix) and an optional `region`, inferred from the ARN when omitted; the response carries `verified` and `topic_arn`, plus `message_sent` on success or `error` on failure.

quotes: | topic_arn | string | Yes | Full SNS topic ARN. Must match arn:aws:sns:<region>:<12-digit-account>:<topic-name> (optional .fifo suffix). |
| region | string | No | AWS region of the topic. If omitted, region is inferred from the ARN. |
"verified": true,
"message_sent": "{\"message\": \"Event Monitoring Message Test\"}"
"error": "<Error that happened while verification>"
"topic_arn": "arn:aws:sns:us-west-2:123456789012:zscaler-em-events",

verify-read-only.statement: The guide calls verification a read-only check of whether Zscaler can call sns:GetTopicAttributes on the topic, with no test message published, although its success example returns a `message_sent` value.

quotes: Use POST /subscriptions/channels/sns:verify to validate that Zscaler can successfully call sns:GetTopicAttributes on your SNS topic. This is a read-only check; no test message is published to the topic.
"message_sent": "{\"message\": \"Event Monitoring Message Test\"}"

verify-codes.statement: sns:verify returns 200 when publish access is validated, 400 for a malformed request or ARN, 404 only for a wrong endpoint path (never for a missing topic), 422 when the request is valid but verification failed at AWS (missing permission, missing topic or another AWS error), and 500 for an internal error.

quotes: | 200 OK | The Zscaler service successfully validated publish access to the SNS topic.
| 400 Bad Request | The request is malformed (e.g., topic_arn is missing or the ARN doesn't match the required regex format).
This code is not used to indicate a missing SNS topic in AWS.
| 422 Unprocessable Entity | The request is syntactically valid, but verification failed at AWS.
| 500 Internal Server Error | Internal error in the Event Monitoring & Notification API service (not caused by the request).
| 404 Not Found | The endpoint URL is incorrect
For example, the Zscaler role does not have permission to call sns:GetTopicAttributes on the topic, the topic doesn't exist, or AWS returned another verification error.

no-delivery-proof.statement: A captured channel schema, or a successful verification, does not show that every channel is enabled for a tenant or that a notification will be delivered; channel availability is per tenant.
no-delivery-proof.conditions: The channel list is described as the channels supported for the tenant, and verification checks topic attributes without publishing.
